10: ## Overview
11: 
12: Tailwind works by scanning your project for utility classes, then generating all of the necessary CSS based on the classes you've actually used.
13: 
14: This makes sure your CSS is as small as possible, and is also what makes features like [arbitrary values](/docs/adding-custom-styles#using-arbitrary-values) possible.
15: 
16: ### How classes are detected
17: 
18: Tailwind treats all of your source files as plain text, and doesn't attempt to actually parse your files as code in any way.
19: 
20: Instead it just looks for any tokens in your file that could be classes based on which characters Tailwind is expecting in class names:
21: 
22: ```jsx
23: // [!code filename:JSX]
24: // [!code word:bg-blue-500]
25: // [!code word:rounded-full]
26: // [!code word:text-white]
27: // [!code word:text-black]
28: // [!code word:font-medium]
29: // [!code word:text-sm\/6]
30: // [!code word:font-sans]
31: // [!code word:bg-black]
32: // [!code word:bg-white]
33: // [!code word:className]
34: // [!code word:function]
35: // [!code word:children]
36: // [!code word:button]
37: // [!code word:shadow]
38: // [!code word:export]
39: // [!code word:colors]
40: // [!code word:color]
41: // [!code word:black]
42: // [!code word:white]
43: // [!code word:const]
44: // [!code word:blue]
45: // [!code word:return]
46: // [!code word:py-1.5]
47: // [!code word:px-2]
48: export function Button({ color, children }) {
49:   const colors = {
50:     black: "bg-black text-white",
51:     blue: "bg-blue-500 text-white",
52:     white: "bg-white text-black",
53:   };
54: 
55:   return (
56:     <button className={`${colors[color]} rounded-full px-2 py-1.5 font-sans text-sm/6 font-medium shadow`}>
57:       {children}
58:     </button>
59:   );
60: }

content.text:
Your original code hit exactly this issue: `bg-[url('{{ Vite::image('hero.jpg') }}')]` isn't a complete, static string at build time—Tailwind scans source files as plain text and can't resolve the Blade interpolation, so the class token doesn't match anything and no CSS is generated (docs/detecting-classes-in-source-files.mdx, "Dynamic class names" section, lines 65–76).

Since the value is fully dynamic (a runtime asset path), Tailwind's arbitrary-value syntax isn't the right tool here — inline `style="background-image: url(...)"` (your working fix) is the documented workaround for values that can't be statically detected.
